name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-three-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 and 3 and receives exact float4 zero from both linked _uber_clear bodies. A five-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected as the result. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel for byte-exact comparison.

name: rope-identity-rotation-permutes-two-strided-half-pairs
rationale: n_batch is 3 and the impl loop also stops at 4, so every reachable loop runs at most three times. offset is 0 and the grid is one thread deep in y, so the rotation angle scale * (offset + pos.y) * inv_freq is exactly 0 for every thread: fast_cos is 1 and fast_sin is 0, and each half pair is copied rather than rotated. That makes the whole 48-byte result exact without depending on a transcendental's low bits. base 4 over a four-thread x grid still drives air.exp2.f32 across -0, -1, -2 and -3, whose exact results 1, 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8 all reach the angle product -- a non-finite exp2 would poison every output through 0 * inf. What the exact bytes pin down is the addressing: strides 8/0/1 and out_strides 2/0/3 read pairs (2*pos.x + 8i, +1) and write pairs (6*pos.x + 2i, +1), so the 24 halves come back permuted and every slot is written.

name: synthesize-merges-for-three-loop-shapes
rationale: Three loop shapes in one kernel, chosen so the structured planner has to SYNTHESIZE merges rather than find them: a nested loop whose inner body has an early break, a four-way switch and a continue and whose outer loop has a second exit; a do-while (bottom-test latch) with two breaks out of it; and a switch with shared case continuations inside a third loop, one of whose arms forces the induction variable past its bound. Measured with llvm-cov over all 959 corpus-backed cased sources plus all 126 other public fixtures, this one module reaches twelve production functions no case and no other fixture reaches: rewrite_switch_bypass_merge in native/cfg/blocks.rs; synth_multi_exit_merge, synth_two_target_dispatch, synth_multi_latch_continue, split_multi_exit_critical_edges and split_two_target_critical_edges in structured_emit/multi_exit.rs; arm_defs_safe_to_clone, privatize_trivial and terminator_mentions in cfg/clone_crossarm/cross_arm.rs; privatize_direct_construct_tree_shared_continuations in structured_emit/straddle.rs; duplicate_phi_incoming in tir/phi_edit.rs; and rename_switch in tir/rename.rs -- the multi-exit funnel, the cross-arm privatizer and the switch-tail splitter. The .ll is the frontend's own lowering of the .metal beside it, not a hand-lowering, so the two halves cannot disagree about what the program is. in[gid] = gid, so v = gid + 7i + 3j sweeps the low bits across lanes and every switch arm, every break and the continue fire on some lane: rounds is 5 on lanes 2-4 and 6 elsewhere (the outer break) and steps is 10 on lanes 0,1,4,5 and 1 on the rest (the two do-while exits), so a merge assigned to the wrong construct moves a counter as well as an accumulator. The last row is never written and must still hold its 0xCD fill.

name: vertex-id-fullscreen-position-instance-zero
rationale: Vertex IDs 0, 1, and 2 generate the oversized full-screen triangle (-1,1), (3,1), and (-1,-3), each with z=w=1. The single instance structurally emits render-target layer zero; the typed position observer records all four covered pixels without authored vertex inputs.

name: stripe-a-vertex-index-map-past-the-byte-that-would-truncate-it
rationale: Each thread narrows its uint2 grid position to a ushort2 and uses both lanes to address four strided slots of a vertex-index map. The 260-wide grid carries tid.x past 255 and 256, so a conversion that keeps only a byte folds the last four threads onto the first four and leaves the top of the map poisoned; the four-of-every-eight stripe the writes leave, and the single untouched word at index 0, pin the layer offset and the layer stride around it.

name: write-a-half-texture-at-a-level-read-from-a-buffer
rationale: Sixteen threads write half4(gid.x, gid.y, 1, 0.5) at texel gid of a 4x4 rgba16_float storage texture at the level lod read from constant ushort buffer 0, through the slot's level views (texture.write indexing the views by the level and dropping a level past the pushed count, DESIGN D230). lod = 0, the texture's only level, so every write is defined: texel (x, y) becomes (x, y, 1, 0.5), all exact in half, and a write that missed its level or texel leaves the 0xab initial bytes. The AIR has no loop.

name: linked-single-radix3-zero-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded radix-3 FFT work item. Unit extents and strides bound every destination-temp write to the authored output. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.

name: reset-irradiance-indirect-count
rationale: The loop-free entry ignores its grid index and unconditionally replaces the complete poisoned four-byte irradiance-cache indirect-entry counter with aligned i32 zero.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-thirteen-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 13 and receives exact float4 zero from all twelve linked _uber_clear bodies. A fifteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: reinterpret-three-local-scratch-views
rationale: Three LOCAL scratch views that reinterpret while they cross the pointer, one per direction of one rule: an equal-width reinterpret is decided by the WIDTH, never by the element type name or the lane count, and the load and store arms must accept the same set or a module cannot read back what it just wrote. (1) A float4 written through a uint[4] scratch -- vector object, scalar-ARRAY pointee whose element type is incompatible but the same width; the load direction already reinterpreted lane-for-lane and the store direction demanded compatible elements. (2) A float[4] scratch read as uint4 -- scalar-SLOT pointee, vector result whose element type is incompatible but the same width; the store direction already reinterpreted lane-for-lane and the load direction demanded compatible elements. (3) A struct whose leading member is half4, read as float2 -- equal TOTAL width, DIFFERENT lane count; the store direction gated on total width and the load direction gated on lane count as well. in[i] is 0x3F800000 + 4i so every word bitcast here is a normal finite float and every half a normal finite half, with no NaN a backend could quieten, so the bits round-trip exactly. Rows 0 and 2 are lane-weighted sums x0 + 2*x1 + 4*x2 + 8*x3, which any permutation of the four lanes moves; rows 1 and 3 are a single middle lane, which pins the actual bits. Row 6 is never written and must still hold its 0xCD fill, so a view that overruns its object is visible.

name: linked-single-unit-average-tmp-input
rationale: Every source, destination, kernel, stride, dilation, and group-count extent is exactly one with zero offsets. The authored temporary input and source are exact one, and the active float destination is table element one, so the bounded large-window completion writes one destination element.

name: tanh-saturates-all-four-half-lanes
rationale:
One invocation with gid (0, 0, 0). The four v9_simple_params bounds are all 1, so every guard passes and the divisor is non-zero; the three strides are authored 7, 11 and 13 against gid lanes that are all zero, so the element index is exactly 0 while a lowering that mixes up a gid lane or a stride would move off it. src holds four distinct half4 elements, so landing on the wrong one changes the bytes instead of reading out of bounds.
air.tanh.v4f16 is an approximation, and the only half arguments whose answer is representable independently of the implementation are the saturations: in binary16 tanh rounds to exactly 1.0 once 1 - tanh(x) falls below 2^-12, which happens past about 4.51. Element 0 is (6, -6, 7, -8), all well past that from both directions -- at 6 the true residual is about 1.2e-5 against a 2.4e-4 rounding threshold, a factor of twenty of margin, so the answer survives whether the backend evaluates tanh in half or in binary32 and converts. That matters because the Metal oracle runs Apple's tanh and the candidate runs whatever MoltenVK recompiles our SPIR-V into. The result (1, -1, 1, -1) is not a palindrome, so reversing the lanes moves the bytes, and a tanh that stops short of one moves all four.

name: linked-k48-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-float-16-non-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes (1 simdgroup) runs the single 16x16 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 16, K = 48 (one whole 32-deep block, the unsafe loader, and a 16-deep remainder, the safe one). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 8 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (expert strides w, scales and biases batch stride = N*K = 768), writing only its own rows. W[e][k][n] (w_ld = 16 bytes): both experts hold q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (all 16 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads); expert 0's scales repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and expert 1's are half of them (biases unread without the bias bit). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . W/2 = a . W): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 16 words observed (64 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Each dequantized weight is a multiple of 0.25 at most 30, exact in float, and each x at most 10; each product with x a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-gather-quantized-matrix-multiply-rhs-float-16-non-transposed
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: The non-transposed float 16 counterpart of the committed mps_gather_qmm_rhs_t_bfloat_64 case (DESIGN D272): mps_gather_qmm_rhs_n_float_16 with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible functions (postfixPrimary_4xf, postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links translation units each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule (D272.4) and the matmul2d lowering (D272.3). Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bins
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. The fixed channel loop advances its literal selector through the entry’s finite component count before exiting; it has no input-dependent trip count. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element, while the exact callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. One-bin histogram parameters force each active channel to bin zero and make the poisoned counters observable byte-exactly.

name: linked-k24-quantized-vector-matrix
rationale: Reaching variant of linked-zero-k cases of this entry (DESIGN D296), whose parameters stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 32 lanes; the user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). The parameters select N = 32 outputs (one threadgroup's 32 columns) over K = 24 rows: the guard (threadgroup_position.y << 5) < N passes, lanes 0 to 23 each dequantize one 8-bit row of W (row stride N bytes) and scale it, the simdgroup sums the 32 partial results, and lane 0 hands all 32 to the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at element indices 0 to 31 (128 bytes, observed whole). x holds 1, 2, 3 repeating, the scales 0.5, 1, 2 repeating, the biases 0 to 3 repeating, and W small integers below 16, so every product and partial sum is an integer multiple of 0.5 far below 2^24: exact in any order or contraction.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-vector-matrix
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: One invocation uses a one-element linked destination array. The authored user constant selects eight-bit quantization, group size one, and zero vector rows; the exact zero K parameter makes both accumulation counts zero. Every arithmetic loop and the final postfix loop is therefore zero-trip, so the poisoned linked destination remains byte-exact while the wrapper and linkage contract execute. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: subsample-a-quarter-luma-through-a-pixel-coordinate-sampler
rationale: Every even texel of a 4x4 ushort image is subsampled through the shader's constant pixel-coordinate sampler and clamped to [0,255]. The four sampled texels each cross the clamp on a different channel, and all twelve texels the kernel must skip hold distinct values under 255, so picking a neighbouring texel or reading the coordinate as normalized gives a different answer on every channel.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-eight-2x2-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 28 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-seven linked _uber_clear bodies. A thirty-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x2 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x2 resource.

name: primitive-id-dual-uint-target-0
rationale: One fullscreen primitive supplies its primitive ID to attachment zero while the entry writes literal 255 to attachment one; this case independently qualifies attachment 0 with both poisoned uint targets bound.

name: primitive-id-dual-uint-target-1
rationale: One fullscreen primitive supplies its primitive ID to attachment zero while the entry writes literal 255 to attachment one; this case independently qualifies attachment 1 with both poisoned uint targets bound.

name: flat-one-pixel-copy
rationale: Function constant texture_layout=0 selects the flat texture2d<half> branch. One invocation reads the deliberate RGBA value (1,1,1,1) from binding 0 through the AIR implicit read sampler and writes the single pixel to poisoned output binding 1.

name: function-constant-flat-one-pixel-half-copy
rationale: Function constant texture_layout=0 structurally selects the flat texture2d<half> operand. One in-bounds invocation copies the deliberate finite RGBA16Float half4 value (1,2,3,4) to the poisoned output texture.

name: eleven-narrow-and-widening-vector-converts
rationale:
Eleven `air.convert` families over sixteen lanes of buffer-supplied operands the Metal compiler cannot fold. Eight of them had no authored case: the narrow vector converts between 8-, 16-, 32- and 64-bit lanes, and float4 to ulong4. Each one is a width or signedness decision a lowering can get exactly backwards, so the lanes name the wrong answer they reject. `uchar3(short3(-1, 255, 511))` is (255, 255, 255) and widening THAT back to short3 is (255, 255), not (-1, -1) -- an unsigned source zero-extends. Beside it `char2` of the same shorts is (-1, -1) and widening THAT to short2 is (-1, -1), not (255, 255) -- a signed source sign-extends. The two sit in one lane so a lowering that picks one rule for both is caught. `short2(uint2)` truncates to the low 16 bits and reads them signed, so 65519 is -17 and 0x8000 is -32768. `uint2(ulong2)` keeps the low 32 bits, so 0xDEADBEEFCAFEBABE is 0xCAFEBABE. float4 to ulong4 truncates toward zero, and the lanes walk 2^32, 2^53, 2^63 and the largest f32 below 2^64 as well as the fractional cases.

The two int-to-half slots are the probe: half saturates at 65504 and its overflow threshold is exactly 65520, so 65519 converts to 0x7BFF and 65520 to infinity, with the negative pair beside them. 2049 and 2051 are exact ties at half precision and round to 2048 and 2052, not 2050 and 2050, so ties-to-even is pinned too. Those two families have 2958 call sites in 624 corpus sources, 540 of which translate, and nothing pinned either boundary. The 209th word is left at the 0xABABABAB fill and read back as an overrun guard.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-four-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2, 3, and 4 and receives exact float4 zero from all three linked _uber_clear bodies. A six-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.
